summary.text: On 18 May 1980, Mount Saint Helens in Washington State, in the United States, had a catastrophic explosive eruption rated 5 on the volcanic explosivity index.
An earthquake made the weakened north face slide away in the largest landslide on land in recorded history, letting gas-rich molten rock burst out northward.
About 57 people were killed, hundreds of square miles became wasteland, and ash fell in 11 American states and several Canadian provinces.

items.prompt: For weeks magma pushed into Mount Saint Helens and its north side swelled. On 18 May, what let the eruption suddenly burst out?

options.label: A lava lake overflowed the summit crater
An earthquake made the north face slide away
Heavy rain soaked into the hot rock
Engineers drilled into the swollen slope

items.explain: An earthquake caused the weakened north face to slide away, releasing the pressurised molten rock behind it.

items.prompt: Mudflows from the eruption reached the Columbia River, nearly 50 miles away. Where did all that water come from?

options.label: A burst dam on a nearby river
A heavy storm that same morning
Melted snow, ice and glaciers on the volcano
Groundwater pumped up by earthquakes

items.explain: The eruption melted snow, ice and several whole glaciers, forming large lahars, or volcanic mudslides.

items.prompt: Before the eruption, part of the north flank was pushed outward. How fast did it grow through late April and early May?

options.label: 5 to 6 feet per day
A few millimetres per year
About a mile per day
Too slowly to be measured

items.explain: The bulge grew by 5 to 6 feet a day and reached more than 400 feet north by mid-May.

items.prompt: Watching the swelling north flank, what did geologists say on 30 April was the greatest immediate danger?

options.label: Lava flowing into nearby towns
Ash poisoning the water supply
A tsunami in the Pacific Ocean
That area sliding and setting off an eruption

items.explain: Geologists warned that sliding of the bulge was the greatest immediate danger and might spark an eruption.

items.prompt: On 27 March, steam explosions blasted a new crater in the old summit. What made the water flash into steam?

options.label: Sunlight melting the summit snow
Magma suddenly heating groundwater
Forest fires burning on the slopes
Friction from small earthquakes

items.explain: These phreatic eruptions happen when magma suddenly heats groundwater, which explodes as steam.

items.prompt: Lightning bolts up to 2 miles long flashed around the volcano during its eruptions. What made them?

options.label: Static electricity from ash clouds
Ordinary thunderstorms over the peak
Power lines broken by the quakes
Hot lava touching the cold glaciers

items.explain: Ash clouds rolling down the volcano built up static electricity that discharged as long lightning bolts.
